To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the S4 region of PKD2-L1 channel is a voltage sensor, and that the voltage dependence of the single-channel conductance is an additional factor that contributes to the voltage dependence of maximal conductance.
the positively charged residues in the putative S4 domain of PKD2-like 1 channels are involved in the voltage-dependent gating of these channels.

the positively-charged S4 residues of the PKD2L-type channel PKD2L are essential to the channel voltage-dependent gating and that the inward-rectification of the single-channel conductance of PKD2 is also voltage-dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the voltage-dependence properties of the PKD2L2 channel and the mechanism underlying its atypical voltage-dependence.
the role of S4 in voltage-dependent gating and its contribution to the atypical voltage-dependence of PKD2.
the voltage-dependent gating properties of the atypical TRP channel PKD2L.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
S4 positively charged residues in PKD2 are involved in the voltage-sensing of PKD2, and the voltage-dependent properties of PKD2 and PKD2L are different.
the positively charged residues in S4 of PKD2-like channels are involved in voltage-sensing.
S4 positively charged residues in PKD2-like channels are not only involved in voltage-sensing, but also play a role in the inward-rectifier property of single-channel conductance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the voltage-dependence and the time-course of activation/deactivation in PKD2-like channels are determined by the charged state of S4.
S4 positively charged residues in PKD2-like channels play a role in the positive shift of the activation curves and the time-courses for activation and deactivation of the channels.
the voltage dependence of PKD2 and its family members is not only due to the voltage sensor in S4, but also the inward rectifier in S1-S4.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of numerical modelling, single-channel conductance measurements, and homology modelling provides a powerful strategy to understand complex voltage-dependent properties of TRP channels.
the S4 region is a key determinant in voltage-dependent gating and that its net positive charges are important for the positive shift in the voltage-dependent activation curve of PKD2-like channels.
the S4 positively charged residues in PKD2-like channels are not involved in the voltage-sensor mechanism, but rather play a role in the regulation of the channel open probability.
